## National vs regional models

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**National**

- One model fitted across Canada
- Shared curve shape ($\beta_2, \beta_3, \beta_4$); strata adjust the asymptote only

:::

::: {.column width="4%"}
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
**Regional**

- Separate model fitted within each region
- Region-specific curve shape
- Captures local patterns but has limited coverage
:::
::::

![](images/eco-strata/national_vs_regional_curve_comparison.png){fig-align="center" width="85%" fig-alt="Paired comparison of national and regional RSYC curves."}

::: notes
National models pool all data across Canada: the curve shape is shared and each stratum
only shifts the asymptote through random effects, which gives stable curves even for
data-poor strata. Regional models are fitted independently within each region, so the
shape of the curve can differ between regions, at the cost of smaller sample sizes.
The examples show that the two fits can diverge (left) or be nearly identical (right).
The package prediction functions use the national curves; regional fits are kept in the
catalogue for comparison.
:::
